title: Slovakia to approve Tesla's self-driving tech
source_used: Drive Tesla Canada (Reuters original returned HTTP 401)
key_facts: Slovakia's transport minister Jozef Ráž said in a social-media video on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026 that Slovakia will formally recognize the Netherlands' provisional approval of Tesla FSD.
That would make Slovakia the ninth EU country to allow FSD; eight already do (Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Slovenia).
Ráž: the driver is still responsible for the car.
The approvals rest on a provisional authorization by Dutch regulator RDW on 10 April 2026.
France, Germany, Italy and Spain have not yet authorized it.
Germany said on 6 Oct that talks with Tesla produced an understanding: FSD capped at 10% over the posted limit.
The EU committee met on 6 Oct and did not vote; December is now the earliest chance for bloc-wide approval.
quote_evidence: The move would allow Tesla owners in Slovakia to use FSD without waiting for an EU-wide authorization.
The EU committee met again on October 6 and despite earlier indications it might approve FSD on that date, didn’t vote.
Eight EU countries already allow the system: Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Lithuania, the Netherlands and Slovenia.
why_it_matters_hint: Each national approval adds support for Tesla's case before the EU-wide vote.
notes: Reuters text (HTTP 401) not read; the Reuters headline matches. Minister's statement, not a completed approval. Follows 7 Oct item X20 on Tesla pressing EU officials.
